title: Make Two Nations Enemies Without Making One Evil

voice.direction: A calm, fair guide who takes neither side. A real question on the hook. Each inscription is read plainly, as a quote, never as an accusation; 'True.' is said with weight, then 'Look what it leaves out' quietly, like noticing something. 'Downstream' mirrors 'Upstream'. The lesson is clear and even; 'neither is evil' lands softly. The tag CTA is friendly. No trailer voice.

lines.text: What if both kingdoms are telling the truth about the same war?
Upstream, the stone says: they crossed the river and burned our town.
True. Look what it leaves out.
Downstream: they dammed the river, and we starved.
True too. It leaves out the fire.
Different losses, stories and values. Enemies, but neither is evil.
Give each side a true story and a real loss, and you'll never need a villain.
Tag someone who loves morally complicated fantasy.

lesson: Two nations can remember the same war truthfully and still disagree, because each lost something different, inherited a different story about it, and holds a different value sacred; each memorial frames out the other side's dead. Enemies are more interesting when both sides have a true story and a real loss: then no villain is needed.
